outcomeNote: Continuous PGO is technically viable and produced broad native-path wins, but the stream guard and profile lifecycle reject it as a product exploit.
changedBeliefs: Exp 054's macOS infrastructure blocker is obsolete on Apple clang 21. `-fprofile-continuous` produced mergeable counters from the Dart-loaded Resqlite dylib without relying on process-exit flushing; generation and use both needed value profiling disabled, and removing absolute source prefixes made the profile reusable across worktrees. The strict profile-use AOT build completed without stale, unprofiled, or backend warnings.

Counter-only PGO can move Resqlite's native wall materially. In a baseline-candidate-candidate-baseline AOT release comparison, batch inserts at 100/1,000/10,000 rows improved 14.6%/12.5%, 16.7%/16.8%, and 19.2%/19.3%; the 10,000 x 20 wide batch improved 12.4%/9.2%, parameterized reads improved 10.6%/10.4%, and multiple rows/selectBytes lanes moved the same direction by roughly 5-13% in both comparisons. The mechanism is real even though the product candidate is rejected.

Broad release wins do not waive a declared narrow latency guard. The preregistered homogeneous-stream kill rule was p50 regression of at least 3% and at least 0.02 ms in at least three of five adjacent 300-trial AOT pairs. Pair p50 deltas were -9.63%, +4.38% (+0.0465 ms), -15.61%, +43.37% (+0.3285 ms), and +11.69% (+0.1315 ms), so pairs 2/4/5 triggered it. The pooled delta was only +1.53% with a confidence interval spanning zero: this is a declared replicated-gate failure amid phase variance, not proof of a stable slowdown.

The measured profile is not a self-contained compiler flag. Its 522,568-byte artifact is tied to the source, Apple clang 21 compatibility contract, target, and representative training corpus; strict profile-use intentionally rejects stale or unprofiled code. Shipping it would require auditable retraining and provenance for every supported target/compiler/source change plus a defined non-PGO fallback. That lifecycle is disproportionate for a lean cross-platform library, so no profile or PGO build-hook path ships.

claims.text: Apple clang 21 continuous instrumentation can generate a usable Resqlite PGO profile from a Dart-loaded dylib. Three representative AOT inputs merged into a 522,568-byte indexed profile covering 2,406 functions, 31,934 blocks, and 2,556,436,455 counter events; strict `-fprofile-use` then built without stale-profile, unprofiled-function, or backend warnings.
claims.conditions: Apple clang/llvm-profdata 21.0.0, Xcode 26.6, arm64 macOS 26.2, Dart 3.12.2, source 02592093e6b6; counter-only continuous mode with atomic updates, value profiling disabled, and stable static-function profile keys; 2026-08-16

claims.text: Representative counter-only PGO produced same-direction broad native-path wins in both comparisons of a B-C-C-B AOT release run: executeBatch at 100/1,000/10,000 rows improved -14.6%/-12.5%, -16.7%/-16.8%, and -19.2%/-19.3%; the 10,000 x 20 wide batch improved -12.4%/-9.2%, parameterized reads -10.6%/-10.4%, and selectBytes at 1,000/10,000 rows -9.2%/-9.3% and -8.6%/-7.9%.
claims.conditions: Separate baseline and PGO AOT native-asset bundles from source 02592093e6b6, baseline-candidate-candidate-baseline order, one full Resqlite-only release pass per arm, same Apple M1 Pro host; 2026-08-16

claims.text: The PGO candidate failed the preregistered homogeneous stream-emission kill rule: p50 regression of at least 3% and at least 0.02 ms in at least three of five adjacent 300-trial AOT pairs. Pair p50 deltas were -9.63%, +4.38% (+0.0465 ms), -15.61%, +43.37% (+0.3285 ms), and +11.69% (+0.1315 ms), so pairs 2/4/5 satisfied both thresholds. The pooled delta was +1.53% with a confidence interval spanning zero; the evidence is a declared replicated-gate failure amid phase variance, not proof of a stable slowdown.
claims.conditions: `benchmark/experiments/stream_rerun_latency.dart --trials=300 --raw`, five adjacent baseline/candidate process pairs, `homogeneous-100small` single-write emission p50, arm64 macOS; predeclared kill rule requires both >=3% and >=0.02 ms candidate regression in >=3/5 pairs; 2026-08-16

nextSignals: Do not repeat exp 054's no-profraw investigation on current Apple toolchains. For a bounded Darwin PGO experiment, start from exp 273's continuous, counter-only recipe and require strict profile-use diagnostics; the exact prototype and indexed profile live only on `archive/exp-273`.

Do not ship a checked-in PGO profile or PGO-enabled build-hook path until there is automated per-target retraining, compiler/source compatibility enforcement, artifact provenance, and an explicit fallback policy. A profile's lifecycle is part of the implementation cost.

Any PGO, LTO, compiler-flag, or code-layout revisit must run five adjacent 300-trial `stream_rerun_latency.dart` pairs and adjudicate the declared homogeneous p50 rule: both >=3% and >=0.02 ms regression in >=3/5 pairs kills the candidate. Report pooled uncertainty too, but do not replace the replicated rule with a post-hoc p95 boundary or pooled-only verdict.

A future PGO revisit needs a materially simpler lifecycle and a profile/training design that clears the same preregistered stream gate without giving back the repeated batch/read/selectBytes gains. Exp 273's pooled +1.53% with a zero-spanning confidence interval limits the claim to gate failure amid phase variance; retuning the corpus after observing that result is a new hypothesis, not a post-hoc rescue.
